author: TEDx Talks
description:
Lethal autonomous weapon systems operate without a 'human in the loop', so who can we hold to account if they are ever used to kill humans?  Dr. Stephanie Hare, co-presenter of the BBC television programme AI Decoded, demonstrates how technology is not neutral, because there is always a human in the loop. Her conclusion: AI can't be put on trial for war crimes, but humans can — and should. Dr. Stephanie Hare is a researcher, broadcaster and author focused on technology, politics and history. 

She co-presents “Artificial Intelligence: Decoded” on BBC television and contributes to the BBC World Service.

Her first book, Technology Is Not Neutral: A Short Guide to Technology Ethics, was named a Financial Times Best Technology Book of summer 2022, and her writing has featured in the Financial Times, The Washington Post, the Guardian/Observer, the Harvard Business Review, WIRED and Computer Weekly. 

She has worked at Accenture, Palantir, and Oxford Analytica; held the Alistair Horne Visi
title: The dark future of AI in war | Stephanie Hare | TEDxBerlin

author: TEDx Talks
description: There's a fountain on Miguel Júdice's family estate in Coimbra that thousands of people visit every year to celebrate eternal love — and he opens his talk by explaining why. It's the true story of his ancestors, Prince Pedro and Inês de Castro: a 14th-century romance forbidden by a king, ended by an assassination, and then, unbelievably, continued after death — Pedro exhumed her body, crowned her queen, and built their tombs foot to foot so they'd see each other first on judgment day. He tells it with real detail and real stakes, then turns it on the audience, asking what a swipe-left culture of situationships might learn from two people who chose each other completely, even past the point of reason. By the end, he leaves you with a challenge simple enough to actually act on: do one meaningful thing for someone you love, today. Come for the history — stay for where he takes it. Miguel Júdice is a hospitality entrepreneur with extensive experience in Portugal's luxury sector. His proje
title: When love lasts eternally: A Portuguese love story | Miguel Júdice | TEDxMarvila

Polina Bibchenko is an outstanding graduate of Beijing Hospitality Institute (BHI) and currently a master’s student at Peking University HSBC Business School. She is a speaker at TEDxBHI. Through choir, a solo singing competition, a coffee-making course, and internship applications, she learned that confidence is not a prerequisite for action. Growth begins when we act before we feel ready. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: Dan Whitlam opens his talk with a line written for someone who doesn't exist yet, then spends the next few minutes being unusually honest about what he's learned about love the hard way — how the way we were held as children becomes the blueprint for how we love as adults, why intimacy is less about touch and more about actually being known, why the friends who've seen every bad version of you and stuck around anyway might be the purest example of love there is. It's a spoken-word set, but it doesn't feel like a performance so much as someone telling you the truth — watch it, and see which of his five rules you didn't know you needed to hear. Dan Whitlam is a poet, rapper, and musician whose work blends reflection, honesty, and emotional depth. After losing his mother young and surviving a stabbing at sixteen, he turned resilience into purpose — using music and poetry to inspire healing and connection. Fresh from his biggest headline tour across North America, Europe, and the UK, and
title: The Five Rules of Love | Dan Whitlam | TEDxMarvila

description: This speaker examines the power of focused social interactions in shifting your perspectives, allowing you to see concepts differently in a way that can greatly improve your ability to do authentic research. Daniel Alland is an entrepreneur currently in his Junior year at Newark Academy. In his free time, he enjoys rock climbing, running, and designing ideas either for fun or as ideas for his next business. Daniel is also a leader in the Outdoors Club and a member of the student AI committee at NA. Daniel values understanding a wide range of ideas and understands that innovation involves making connections between people and between concepts. In his TedX talk, Daniel shares one technique he uses to gain understanding when making these connections. author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores the beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors that enable people to become proactive creators of opportunities rather than passive observers of circumstances. The talk challenges the traditional idea that entrepreneurship begins with an idea, capital, or a business plan. Instead, it proposes that entrepreneurship begins with a decision: to think differently and take responsibility for creating the future.

Through practical insights and real-world examples, the talk introduces the essential elements of an entrepreneurial mindset vision, action, resilience, innovation, discipline, adaptability, and purpose and shows how these principles can be applied not only to business, but also to education, professional careers, and everyday life. Cecilia María Jáuregui Gamarra is a Bolivian industrial engineer, entrepreneur, and environmental leader. She is the founder and General Manager of INNOVAPLAST, an ecological plastics company based in El Alto, La Paz, focused on recycling plas
title: Unstoppable: The Code of the Entrepreneurial Mindset | Cecilia Jauregui | TEDxUnivalle La Paz

author: TEDx Talks
description: "What's the difference between a cardiac surgeon and God?" Professor José Fragata opens with the punchline: "God does not think he is a cardiac surgeon." It's the first laugh in a talk built on forty years and nearly 4,000 operations on hearts no bigger than a walnut. But the real turning point is personal — early in his career, he and his wife learned their own daughter needed heart surgery. She's in the audience today, alive and well. From that moment on, he says, he understood the twin values that define his work: humanity and humility, "two faces of the same coin." Watch to hear the moment he shows a blue newborn his own pink fingernails for the first time — and why he believes you can cure a patient with technology, but it takes a human heart to heal one. Professor José Fragata is a distinguished academic cardiothoracic surgeon, former head of department, and full professor of surgery, now retired. His career spans more than 45 years, during which he performed thousands of cardia
title: Humanity and humility in children’s heart surgery | José I. G. Fragata | TEDxMarvila

description: This speaker shares his experiences with the world’s most popular board game—chess—with a little twist. By bridging principles of quantum mechanics with the game he loves, Surya will explore how Quantum Chess reshaped his approach to uncertainty, decision-making, and life itself. Surya, a sophomore at Newark Academy, is passionate about many areas of STEM, with math at the heart of everything he does, alongside a deep interest in physics and computer science. As a competitive math student, he has participated in numerous national and international math tournaments, continuously pushing himself at the highest level. He is deeply committed to giving back, whether through volunteering as a math tutor with the OneInMath Program, raising funds for homeless youth, or brightening lives through Color A Smile. Outside of academics, he performs with the New Jersey Youth Symphony's Youth Orchestra and competes on NA's Varsity Swim team. Surya is excited to bring his passion for math and emerging
title: Quantum Chess: A New Lens on Uncertainty | Surya Raghavan | TEDxNewark Academy

author: TEDx Talks
description: Is sharing a meal ever just eating? Restaurateur Suzana Barros doesn't think so. From a Portuguese painting of two lovers lost in conversation over dinner, to her childhood table set every night by candlelight, to the first-date jitters and quiet business deals she watches unfold nightly at her Lisbon restaurant Tágide — she makes the case that every meal carries something invisible: care, memory, belonging. But she doesn't stop at comfort. Drawing on centuries of art history, from tender family scenes to a 16th-century painting of hell itself, she shows how the same table that nourishes love has also hosted excess, power, even poison. So what is food, really — care, power, love, or something more dangerous? Watch to find out why Barros believes the answer isn't fixed. It's a choice we make every time we sit down. Suzana Barros is an art expert, entrepreneur, restaurateur, and ceramist whose work bridges creativity, culture, and community. With degrees from ESAD and Sotheby's Institut
title: Love and Gastronomy: Union or Ambivalence? | Suzana Barros | TEDxMarvila

You don’t need perfect English or a perfect life to be heard—you just need to be real. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Comment peut-on avancer quand on a dû prendre la décision de partir du jour au lendemain, à contrecœur ? À quoi se raccrocher quand on a perdu ses racines et que plus rien n’est stable autour de nous ?

C’est à ces questions, et à bien d’autres, que répond Viktoriya Kilitauri, ukrainienne arrivée en France en 2014, dans son interview pour TEDxChâteauroux.
 À travers son témoignage et son parcours de vie semé d’obstacles, avant son départ, pendant son voyage, puis à son arrivée en France avec un simple visa espagnol, Viktoriya nous livre un message d’espoir. 

Elle raconte comment elle a puisé dans sa foi en l’humanité et dans l’amour de ses proches, mais aussi comment elle a noué des liens avec les personnes qui lui ont tendu la main, pour reconstruire sa vie loin de ses racines.

Aujourd’hui, Viktoriya joue un rôle de « passeuse » : elle transmet son expérience et son vécu en accompagnant les ukrainiens qui arrivent dans le département de l’Indre. Elle joue un rôle de médiatrice dans
title: De la Crimée à Châteauroux : quand le voyage s’impose | Viktoriya Kilitauri | TEDxChâteauroux

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Plongez au cœur de la Brenne, au bord de l’étang du Couvent à Saint-Michel-en-Brenne, à l'occasion du TEDxChâteauroux. 

Quentin Giraud, ornithologue et chargé de mission à l'association Indre Nature, et Tristan Dejust, chargé d’études en bioacoustique à la Réserve naturelle nationale de Chérine, s'associent pour vous faire découvrir l'un des joyaux les plus secrets et menacés de notre patrimoine naturel : les marouettes. Dissimulées dans une végétation aquatique très dense et actives principalement la nuit, la Marouette ponctuée, la Marouette poussin et la Marouette de Baillon sont quasiment impossibles à observer à l'œil nu. Pour relever le défi de leur suivi, les deux structures ont déployé une méthode novatrice mêlant écologie de terrain et technologies de pointe à l'échelle du Parc naturel régional de la Brenne.

Grâce à un réseau de plus de 50 boîtiers enregistreurs AudioMoth — protégés par des coques conçues sur mesure en impression 3D avec un fablab local —, des dizaines de mi
title: L'IA pour étudier et préserver les espèces | Tristan Dejust & Quentin Giraud | TEDxChâteauroux

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, I reflect on a question that stayed with me for years: Can caregiving and leadership truly coexist?

Through my experience as a senior technology product manager and a parent to a child with complex needs, I began to notice something unexpected—many of the leadership skills I rely on at work were developed much earlier, in real-world situations that required navigating ambiguity, aligning across stakeholders, and making decisions without formal authority.

These experiences didn’t replace formal training or professional growth, but they shaped how I approach complex problems and collaboration today.

This talk is an attempt to broaden how we recognize leadership, by looking not just at titles, but at the underlying skills and responsibilities that define it. Punit Kaur is a product management leader, speaker, and musician who brings a deeply human lens to leadership. A Harvard-trained product manager and mother to a child with special needs, she reframes caregiving
title: The leaders we overlook | Punit Kaur | TEDxNorthwesternU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"What if the foundational anchor of your life isn't fixed, but entirely yours to choose?

In this insightful and reflective talk, The Life Between Two Notes, Kabir Khanuja uses the philosophy of Indian classical music to reimagine how we navigate existence. In music, no note has an inherent identity any pitch you choose can become the Sa (the root tonic), redefining the emotional color and resonance of every note that follows. Kabir translates this elegant principle to the human experience, exploring how shifting our primary reference points can transform our perspective, purpose, and relationship with uncertainty.

Whether you are navigating change, searching for balance, or trying to find meaning in the quiet spaces between life's major milestones, this talk is a profound reminder that harmony is not something you stumble into, it is something you compose. Kabir Khanuja is a Computer Science student at VIT Pune, a musician, and a curious explorer at the intersection of technology an
title: The Life Between Two Notes | Kabir Khanuja | TEDxVIT Pune

description: Life rarely follows the path we chart for it. It throws curveballs, changes direction and sometimes leaves us at crossroads. But a sudden pivot doesn’t have to be a dead end. It can be an invitation to find another way. Through a series of unexpected personal and professional turns, this talk explores what happens when the path you planned is no longer an option, and how new possibilities can emerge when you choose to move forward. Because you don’t always have to know where the road leads. Sometimes, all that’s needed is that one step forward. Ruth Dsouza Prabhu is a Bengaluru-based independent journalist, author, and content developer with 25 years of experience across television, print and digital media. Her international bylines span The New York Times, Al Jazeera and Nikkei Asia, alongside top-tier Indian publications including Mint Lounge, Condé Nast Traveller, The Hindu and Travel & Leisure, among several others. An award-winning food and features writer, she is the author of I

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As AI moves from the digital world into the physical world, the relationship between humans and intelligence is also changing. The question we need to ask is no longer who will replace whom, but how humans and AI can augment one another. This talk explores how Physical AI can bring intelligence into cities, spaces, and everyday life, while advances in brain science open new possibilities for enhancing human cognition. These two paths ultimately converge toward a future of Human plus AI—where humans and intelligent systems augment one another and evolve together.
当 AI 从数字世界走向现实世界，人类与智能的关系也正在发生改变。我们需要思考的，不再是谁替代谁，而是谁增强谁。本次演讲从 Physical AI 出发，探讨智能如何进入城市、空间与生活；同时从脑科学出发，探索如何增强人类自身的认知能力。两条进化路线最终汇合，走向一个 Human plus AI 的未来——人类与智能彼此增强，共同进化。
 远筑集团董事长，IMBIU 的创始人 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We live in a world where content is infinite, attention is limited, and AI can create almost anything in seconds.

So, when everyone can create, speak and publish, what becomes truly valuable?

In this TEDx talk, Poonam Nikam explores the changing nature of communication, the rise of AI, and how Gen Z is reshaping the way we decide whom to trust.

From personal experiences in communication to the growing influence of trusted communities, this talk explores a simple but powerful idea:

Technology has made information abundant. It has not made trust abundant.

As content becomes easier to create, trust becomes harder to earn and more valuable than ever.

In the age of possibilities, trust may be the ultimate currency.
 Poonam Nikam leads communications strategy across India and APAC for Snapchat, one of the world’s most culturally influential platforms. With a career spanning consumer technology, music, lifestyle, and telecommunications, she brings creative instinct and strategic rigour
title: In the age of infinite content, trust is the new currency | Poonam Nikam | TEDxSukhna Lake

description: This TEDx Talk explores how many of our life choices are shaped not by what we truly want, but by social expectations, peer pressure, and inherited beliefs. Like a black box, we see the inputs and the outputs, yet rarely question the code that connects them. The talk invites us to pause, examine who wrote our code, and consciously choose whether we want to keep living on autopilot, or rewrite the code  it ourselves. Navya Singla is a Grade XI student whose curiosity lies at the crossroads of technology and human behaviour. Fascinated by robotics and artificial intelligence, he enjoys exploring how algorithms, patterns, and code can offer deeper insights into the way people think and make decisions. Believing that technology is as much about understanding people as it is about solving problems, Navya hopes to inspire others to question the invisible code that shapes their lives and become conscious architects of their own future. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED confer
title: Living In Blackbox Life- Who Wrote Your Code? | Navya Singla | TEDxMRIS Charmwood Youth

description:
Most people think the biggest risk is failing... it's not. It's standing still and calling that stability. Andre Lokuszta shows how the biases we trust most quietly erode the lives of people who believe they're being responsible. Failure is a correction, but stagnation? That's the real cost. Andre Lokuszta studies Business Psychology at UC San Diego and founded Netcast Marketing at 17 to solve a problem most companies walk away from: deploying AI-powered growth infrastructure for industries where a single compliance misstep means an SEC examination. His firm works with independent financial advisors, building the systems that turn regulatory barriers into competitive advantages. Across his client portfolio, he has generated over $7 million in revenue and an average 5x return on investment.

What if education was never meant to be about getting everything right?

In this talk, Dr. Arijit Roy questions a system that often places marks, memorisation and perfection above curiosity. He invites teachers to rethink the classroom—not as a place where knowledge is simply delivered, but as a space where teachers and students learn, question and grow together.

From celebrating mistakes to going beyond marks, the talk explores how small shifts in the way we teach can create fearless thinkers.

Because the goal of education is not perfection.

It is possibility. Popularly known as “Rancho Sir,” inspired by Three Idiots, Dr. Arijit has spent over 15 years reimagining education through curiosity, creativity, and courage. To his students, he is “Dada”—a mentor and guide who inspires them to think beyond boundaries. title: The MAGIC Indian Classroom Needs | Dr. Arijit Roy | TEDxMLAC Women

In this talk, Blake Murphy explores the intersection of data and storytelling, drawing on his experience in sports media to show how information becomes meaningful when it is shaped into a compelling human narrative. In an age of overwhelming information, he asks us to consider whether the real power of data lies not in the numbers themselves, but in the stories we choose to tell with them. Blake Murphy is a host, writer, and analyst for Sportsnet, covering the Toronto Raptors and Toronto Blue Jays. Originally pursuing a path in business and law, he ultimately found his way into sports media, where he combines data-driven analysis with reporting and storytelling. Across multiple sports and platforms, Blake helps audiences make sense of the numbers behind the game while keeping the people and stories at the centre. This
title: Art of WAR: Remaining People-Focused in Data Storytelling | Blake Murphy | TEDxUBC

Riana Thadani, a type 1 diabetic of over 10 years, challenges the misconceptions and stereotypes that surround her condition.
